project.name: aih-ui
project.description: Policy Workbench user interface for AIH, built as an independent browser application with a design prototype, a composed app shell with catalog and governance features, and a local preview server with contract and acceptance check scripts. Policy logic, catalog content and scanner execution stay in the public @aihq/core, @aihq/catalog and @aihq/scan packages.

nodes.name: dom.js
nodes.summary: Shared DOM primitives (text normalization, element creation via textContent, and fail-loud id lookup) used by every UI component so package data is never parsed as HTML.

nodes.name: text
nodes.summary: Normalizes a value to a non-empty string or null, treating empty and undefined as absence.

nodes.name: el
nodes.summary: Creates a DOM element with an optional class and text content set safely via textContent.

nodes.name: collectIds
nodes.summary: Looks up a list of element ids and returns them camelCase-keyed, throwing on the first missing element.

nodes.name: cards.js
nodes.summary: Renders the catalog grid: one card per visible entry with kind icon, publisher title and description, curated or declared category badge, and placeholder scan/token slots that say Not published.

nodes.name: badgeOf
nodes.summary: Chooses a card's category badge from Catalog's curated category or the upstream-declared category.

nodes.name: card
nodes.summary: Builds one catalog card with header, publisher description and footer slots for scan status, token estimate and a disabled allow toggle.

nodes.name: createCards
nodes.summary: Creates the cards grid component that renders visible entries and the visible count caption.

nodes.name: categories.js
nodes.summary: Rebinds Catalog's curated category records to served index entries and exposes badge, note and count helpers, never inferring categories that Catalog did not curate.

nodes.name: applyCategories
nodes.summary: Binds served curated category records to index entries by entry id and subject digest, returning state, taxonomy and a per-entry map.

nodes.name: curatedCategoryOf
nodes.summary: Returns the curated category record for an entry, if any.

nodes.name: curationNote
nodes.summary: Produces the tooltip note explaining a category is curated by Catalog maintainers.

nodes.name: categoryBadge
nodes.summary: Builds the badge label and title for an entry's curated category or Not curated.

nodes.name: categoryRows
nodes.summary: Counts curated categories across entries into sorted rows for display.

nodes.name: collections.js
nodes.summary: Applies Catalog's published collection view to the index to decide which entries are current inventory, counting older entries only as diagnostics.

nodes.name: applyCollections
nodes.summary: Filters index entries to current inventory using Catalog's collection membership and subject digests, reporting non-current entries as diagnostics.

nodes.name: controller.js
nodes.summary: Sources & Catalogs feature controller that owns the single selection/filter state, loads the catalog, and wires all catalog components through models and callbacks.

nodes.name: createCatalog
nodes.summary: Creates the catalog feature: loads data, holds view/selection state, and renders cards, details, metrics, navigation, provenance and toolbar on each change.

nodes.name: details.js
nodes.summary: Renders the inspector's Details and Security tabs: publisher overview, declared capabilities, upstream provenance, evidence statements and Catalog qualification, with explicit absence wording.

nodes.name: row
nodes.summary: Builds a labelled key/value row for the inspector details panes.

nodes.name: capability
nodes.summary: Renders one declared-capability row, distinguishing Not declared from Not published.

nodes.name: renderQualification
nodes.summary: Renders the Security tab's qualification block with state, receipt window, signature and attestation.

nodes.name: createDetails
nodes.summary: Creates the inspector component that renders the Details and Security tabs for the selected entry.

nodes.name: elements.js
nodes.summary: Looks up all Sources & Catalogs DOM elements once and groups them per owning component so no component queries the DOM itself.

nodes.name: catalogElements
nodes.summary: Collects all catalog DOM ids and groups them by owning component (provenance, navigation, toolbar, grid, inspector).

nodes.name: entry.js
nodes.summary: Pure readers over a single published catalog entry: source identity by source type, digests, labels, evidence statements, kind icons and search text.

nodes.name: shortDigest
nodes.summary: Shortens a sha256 digest for compact display.

nodes.name: sourceIdentity
nodes.summary: Reads an entry's source identity according to its source.type discriminator (github, npm, aih).

nodes.name: sourceLabelOf
nodes.summary: Returns a short display label for an entry's source.

nodes.name: sourceLabelTitle
nodes.summary: Returns a descriptive tooltip for an entry's source label.

nodes.name: sourceDetailRows
nodes.summary: Builds the detail rows describing an entry's upstream source per source type.

nodes.name: identity
nodes.summary: Returns an entry's displayable identity fields (name, kind, ids, digest).

nodes.name: statement
nodes.summary: Normalizes a single evidence statement from an entry.

nodes.name: statementsOf
nodes.summary: Lists an entry's evidence statements with summaries as Catalog's reader returns them.

nodes.name: firstSummary
nodes.summary: Returns the first available statement summary for an entry.

nodes.name: searchText
nodes.summary: Builds the lowercase searchable text for an entry from its identity, source and publisher fields.

nodes.name: index-source.js
nodes.summary: Loads the served @aihq/catalog index and preview summary, enforces the index format/version contract, and applies collections, publisher, qualification and category sidecars.

nodes.name: loadJson
nodes.summary: Fetches and parses a served JSON document, raising a descriptive error on failure.

nodes.name: loadCatalog
nodes.summary: Loads the catalog index and summary, validates the contract, and applies collections, publisher, qualification and category data.

nodes.name: metrics.js
nodes.summary: Renders the six-kind ledger metric tiles above the split, counting only kinds the index carries and showing Not published for the rest.

nodes.name: tile
nodes.summary: Builds one ledger metric tile, clickable only for kinds the index counts.

nodes.name: createMetrics
nodes.summary: Creates the metric tiles component that renders the six-kind ledger.

nodes.name: navigation.js
nodes.summary: Renders the left-rail Catalog Scopes: one row per published source identity or Catalog collection, with revision markers, curated category breakdown and organization additions.

nodes.name: badgeNode
nodes.summary: Builds a small badge element for a scope row.

nodes.name: categoriesReason
nodes.summary: Explains why curated categories are unavailable for a scope.

nodes.name: curatedCategories
nodes.summary: Renders the curated category breakdown under the selected source row.

nodes.name: scopeRow
nodes.summary: Renders one source or collection scope row with count, revision and selection state.

nodes.name: additionsRow
nodes.summary: Renders the organization's own additions row, empty until something is imported.

nodes.name: createNavigation
nodes.summary: Creates the left-rail navigation component listing catalog scopes.

nodes.name: provenance.js
nodes.summary: Renders the installed-package provenance strip, the masthead naming the selected source, and the source status line, stating unconnected organization/Core state explicitly.

nodes.name: createProvenance
nodes.summary: Creates the provenance component rendering the package strip, masthead and source status line with diagnostic details.

nodes.name: publisher.js
nodes.summary: Rebinds Catalog's publisher presentation metadata (titles, descriptions, categories) to index entries and reads it back with Catalog's own unavailability reasons.

nodes.name: applyPublisher
nodes.summary: Binds served publisher metadata records to index entries, keeping the reader's refusal reason when unavailable.

nodes.name: publisherOf
nodes.summary: Returns the publisher record for an entry, if bound.

nodes.name: categoryCoverage
nodes.summary: Counts how many entries carry an upstream-declared category.

nodes.name: publishedText
nodes.summary: Returns a published publisher value or null, never inventing text.

nodes.name: provenanceNote
nodes.summary: Explains where a publisher value came from or why it is missing.

nodes.name: qualification.js
nodes.summary: Rebinds Catalog's publisher qualification reader results to index entries, with tooltips for each state word and attestation sentences, never treating qualified as approval.

nodes.name: attestationSentence
nodes.summary: Describes the attestation state of a qualification in words.

nodes.name: applyQualification
nodes.summary: Binds qualification reader records to index entries by entry id and subject digest.

nodes.name: qualificationOf
nodes.summary: Returns the qualification record for an entry, if bound.

nodes.name: selectors.js
nodes.summary: Pure presentation selectors for search, filtering, sorting, inventory counts and source scopes, computing every displayed number from the installed index at run time.

nodes.name: sourceFilterValue
nodes.summary: Encodes a source filter value from type, identity and revision.

nodes.name: matchesSourceFilter
nodes.summary: Tests whether an entry matches a nested source filter.

nodes.name: visibleEntries
nodes.summary: Applies search, kind, source filters and sorting to produce the visible entries.

nodes.name: sortedCounts
nodes.summary: Sorts a count map into descending rows.

nodes.name: inventoryCounts
nodes.summary: Computes kind, source-type and scope counts from the installed entries.

nodes.name: sourceScopes
nodes.summary: Groups entries into source identity and collection scopes with counts and revisions.

nodes.name: scopeCountOf
nodes.summary: Returns the item count for a scope.

nodes.name: collectionOf
nodes.summary: Returns the Catalog collection an entry is a current member of.

nodes.name: selectedScope
nodes.summary: Resolves the currently selected scope from the view.

nodes.name: scopeEntries
nodes.summary: Returns entries belonging to the selected scope.

nodes.name: scopeTotal
nodes.summary: Returns the item total for the selected scope.

nodes.name: describeCollection
nodes.summary: Describes a collection scope with owner, release and package-mismatch marker.

nodes.name: describeScope
nodes.summary: Describes a source scope's label, revision and details for navigation and masthead.

nodes.name: toolbar.js
nodes.summary: Renders the filter toolbar: the primary review pills (with unavailable Needs Review/Egress Out) and secondary kind, source-type and sort controls with scroll affordance.

nodes.name: reviewPill
nodes.summary: Builds a primary review pill, disabled with a reason when no data can back its count.

nodes.name: kindPill
nodes.summary: Builds a kind filter pill with its count and active state.

nodes.name: createToolbar
nodes.summary: Creates the toolbar component rendering review pills, kind pills, search, source filter and sort.

nodes.name: view-state.js
nodes.summary: Persists the catalog view (query, filters, sort) in sessionStorage and restores it validated against the installed index counts.

nodes.name: emptyView
nodes.summary: Returns the default empty catalog view.

nodes.name: saveView
nodes.summary: Saves the view to sessionStorage, ignoring blocked storage.

nodes.name: restoreView
nodes.summary: Restores a saved view, dropping filters and sort keys the installed index does not publish.

nodes.name: publisher-refusal.test.mjs
nodes.summary: Node test suite verifying that a refused publisher-metadata sidecar is reported with the reader's reason rather than as Catalog publishing nothing.

nodes.name: absence.js
nodes.summary: Defines the shared absence vocabulary (Not published, Not declared, Not supplied, Not connected) and related reason strings so the UI never conflates missing package data with missing operator input.

nodes.name: bytes.js
nodes.summary: Moves exact artifact bytes between files, the backend and browser downloads via Base64 without re-serializing, preserving the canonical bytes Core's parsers require.

nodes.name: bytesToBase64
nodes.summary: Encodes a byte array to a Base64 string without re-serialization.

nodes.name: base64ToBytes
nodes.summary: Decodes a Base64 string back into the exact original bytes.

nodes.name: downloadBase64
nodes.summary: Triggers a browser download of Base64-encoded bytes under a given filename.

nodes.name: controller.js
nodes.summary: Governance workflow controller that wires all pane components and transport calls into one vertical slice (select, inspect, import evidence, prepare, save, reopen, consume) while guarding every async answer with revision tokens so verdicts only reflect current inputs.

nodes.name: createGovernance
nodes.summary: Builds the Governance pane: instantiates all components, holds workflow state, and orchestrates prepare, store, reopen and consume calls with revision-guarded async handling.

nodes.name: detector.js
nodes.summary: Renders scanner attestation, scanner result facts and detector provenance as three distinct statements in the Governance pane.

nodes.name: renderScanResult
nodes.summary: Renders the scanner attestation, scan result facts and detector provenance sections for a scan result.

nodes.name: createDetector
nodes.summary: Creates the detector component that displays scanner attestation and provenance state.

nodes.name: elements.js
nodes.summary: Collects the Governance pane's DOM elements by id and groups them by the component that owns each one.

nodes.name: governanceElements
nodes.summary: Looks up all Governance pane element ids and returns them grouped per owning component.

nodes.name: inputs.js
nodes.summary: Component owning the subject readout, catalog details, evidence file input and decision/target/effect/route fields; exposes operator-supplied values without ever inventing missing ones.

nodes.name: renderCatalog
nodes.summary: Renders published catalog information about the selected subject.

nodes.name: setTargetOptions
nodes.summary: Populates the target select options from the subject's available targets.

nodes.name: createInputs
nodes.summary: Creates the inputs component managing subject readout, evidence file and decision fields, exposing values().

nodes.name: observation.js
nodes.summary: Component collecting the operator's observation inputs (artifact manifest, install root and folder) and handing the bytes to the backend by path without parsing or hashing them.

nodes.name: createObservation
nodes.summary: Creates the observation component collecting manifest, install root and folder inputs.

nodes.name: operator-files.js
nodes.summary: Component for the operator's own authority, verifier trust and attestation material files, stored separately and never derived from imported evidence.

nodes.name: createOperatorFiles
nodes.summary: Creates the component handling authority, verifier trust and attestation file inputs.

nodes.name: prepared.js
nodes.summary: Component owning the Prepare button, the prepared-artifact readout and exact-byte downloads, showing binding only as a claim until independent consumption.

nodes.name: createPrepared
nodes.summary: Creates the prepared-artifact component with Prepare button, readout and download buttons.

nodes.name: reopen.js
nodes.summary: Component that reopens the two downloaded files in a fresh session so consumption re-derives the verdict independently from the exact bytes.

nodes.name: createReopen
nodes.summary: Creates the reopen component that accepts the downloaded files for a fresh independent session.

nodes.name: revisions.js
nodes.summary: Revision tracker that assigns a revision per verification input slot and session so asynchronous answers minted under stale inputs are discarded.

nodes.name: createRevisionTracker
nodes.summary: Creates a per-slot revision tracker issuing tokens and checking whether an answer's token is still current.

nodes.name: rows.js
nodes.summary: Provides the single label/value row renderer used across Governance displays, rendering null values as an explicit absence word.

nodes.name: row
nodes.summary: Appends a label/value row to a parent element, showing the given absence word when the value is null.

nodes.name: statuses.js
nodes.summary: Renders the six verification status axes as six separate cells in contract order, never collapsing them into one badge.

nodes.name: createStatuses
nodes.summary: Creates the statuses component rendering all six verification axes as separate cells.

nodes.name: transport.js
nodes.summary: HTTP transport layer for every Governance call to the preview backend's /api endpoints, passing operator input through unchanged and returning Core's answers.

nodes.name: api
nodes.summary: Posts a JSON body to a backend /api path and normalizes network and error responses.

nodes.name: fetchSubject
nodes.summary: Requests the published subject information for a catalog selection.

nodes.name: fetchCatalogIntegrity
nodes.summary: Requests catalog integrity information from the backend.

nodes.name: parseEvidence
nodes.summary: Sends evidence bytes to the backend for parsing by Core.

nodes.name: prepare
nodes.summary: Asks the backend to prepare an artifact through Core from operator inputs.

nodes.name: storeOperatorFile
nodes.summary: Stores one operator file (authority, trust or attestation) in the session.

nodes.name: storeObservation
nodes.summary: Stores the operator's observation manifest and files in the session.

nodes.name: reopenFromFiles
nodes.summary: Opens a fresh session from the downloaded files.

nodes.name: consume
nodes.summary: Requests independent consumption of the saved artifact and returns the verdict.

nodes.name: loadValidationFixture
nodes.summary: Loads the explicitly labelled validation fixture.

nodes.name: fetchSaved
nodes.summary: Fetches the exact saved bytes for download.

nodes.name: verdict.js
nodes.summary: Component owning the Consume button and verdict readout, including assessment binding, observation results and the mandatory execution sentence.

nodes.name: createVerdict
nodes.summary: Creates the verdict component with the Consume button and verdict readout.

nodes.name: executionSentence
nodes.summary: Chooses the execution sentence for not-attempted, observed or refused execution values.

nodes.name: renderAssessmentBinding
nodes.summary: Renders the assessment binding details of a verdict.

nodes.name: renderObservation
nodes.summary: Renders the observation result details of a verdict.

nodes.name: vocabulary.js
nodes.summary: Defines the words the Governance pane may use: the six status axes, tone mappings and refusal wording, with rules forbidding Applied/Installed/Executed language.

nodes.name: refusalWording
nodes.summary: Maps a refusal code to the permitted user-facing wording.

nodes.name: revisions.test.mjs
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the revision tracker covering slot tokens, session changes, selection changes and undefined-slot errors.

nodes.name: scan-attribution-cases.mjs
nodes.summary: Acceptance cases for Scan signer attribution: signs a fixture with the second of two trusted keys carrying different operator declarations, reorders roots, and asserts the verifier attributes the declaration of the actual signer.

nodes.name: artifacts.mjs
nodes.summary: Exact-byte artifact I/O for the backend worker: base64 helpers, byte-exact read/write/copy of files and trees, JSON file helpers, and session-relative path naming so the page never sees machine paths.

nodes.name: catalog-access.mjs
nodes.summary: Reads the installed @aihq/catalog through Catalog's published content reader, resolving the package root, looking up entries, joining descriptor paths safely, and reporting Catalog's own integrity result.

nodes.name: catalog-assessment.mjs
nodes.summary: Builds the optional assessment resolver handed to Core, supplying only the published Catalog assessment artifact bytes for the identity Core derived.

nodes.name: catalog-categories.mjs
nodes.summary: Serves Catalog's curated per-entry categories through readCatalogCategoriesV1, reporting refusals rather than assigning or inferring categories.

nodes.name: catalog-collections.mjs
nodes.summary: Serves Catalog's current collection view through readCatalogCollectionsV1, bound to the exact index bytes; loaded on demand by the worker.

nodes.name: catalog-publisher.mjs
nodes.summary: Serves publisher titles, descriptions and categories from Catalog's display-only presentation sidecar via readCatalogPresentationV1, reporting unavailable values with Catalog's reason.

nodes.name: catalog-qualification.mjs
nodes.summary: Serves Catalog's publisher qualification states via readCatalogQualificationV1, which re-verifies the shipped signed head and receipts, stamped with the instant they hold at.

nodes.name: makeSigner
nodes.summary: Generates an Ed25519 key pair and returns a signer with its Scan key id and public key for a test case.

nodes.name: writeTrust
nodes.summary: Writes an operator trust file with the given roots and expectations into the case directory.

nodes.name: consumeWith
nodes.summary: Runs buildScanVerification against scan material and a trust file and returns the attributed operator provenance.

nodes.name: b64
nodes.summary: Encodes bytes as base64.

nodes.name: fromB64
nodes.summary: Decodes a base64 string into a Buffer.

nodes.name: sessionRelativePath
nodes.summary: Returns a POSIX session-relative name for a file inside a session directory, or undefined when it has none.

nodes.name: writeExactBytes
nodes.summary: Writes bytes exactly as given, creating parent directories.

nodes.name: readExactBytes
nodes.summary: Reads a file's exact bytes without re-serialization.

nodes.name: recreateDirectory
nodes.summary: Removes and recreates a directory to get a clean root.

nodes.name: copyExactTree
nodes.summary: Recursively copies a directory tree byte for byte.

nodes.name: readJsonFile
nodes.summary: Reads and parses a JSON file.

nodes.name: writeJsonFile
nodes.summary: Serializes a value to a JSON file (used for non-artifact operator files).

nodes.name: catalogRoot
nodes.summary: Resolves the installed @aihq/catalog package root through package resolution.

nodes.name: readCatalog
nodes.summary: Reads and validates the content index through readCatalogContentV1, optionally verifying artifact hashes.

nodes.name: catalogEntry
nodes.summary: Looks up one catalog entry by id, refusing when it is absent.

nodes.name: artifactPath
nodes.summary: Joins a descriptor path under the Catalog root through resolveCatalogContentPathV1.

nodes.name: entryContentDir
nodes.summary: Resolves the content directory of an entry within the Catalog package.

nodes.name: catalogIntegrity
nodes.summary: Reports Catalog's own artifact integrity result for an entry without restating its rules.

nodes.name: createCatalogAssessmentResolver
nodes.summary: Returns a resolver that supplies the published assessment artifact bytes for exactly one matching aih entry, or nothing.

nodes.name: catalogCategories
nodes.summary: Reads curated categories through Catalog's reader and returns them or the refusal.

nodes.name: catalogCollections
nodes.summary: Reads the current collection view through Catalog's reader against the index bytes.

nodes.name: catalogPublisher
nodes.summary: Reads publisher presentation records through Catalog's reader, reporting unavailability when the contract is missing.

nodes.name: catalogQualification
nodes.summary: Reads per-entry qualification through Catalog's qualification reader at the current instant and serves its words verbatim.

nodes.name: catalog-served.mjs
nodes.summary: Projects the output of Catalog's public content reader member by member into the document served to the page, so no field the reader drops can reach the UI.

nodes.name: core-adapter.mjs
nodes.summary: Calls @aihq/core's public API for subject derivation, evidence parsing, preparation and independent consumption of governance input, wiring in the Catalog assessment resolver and Scan verification without reproducing Core logic.

nodes.name: core-service.mjs
nodes.summary: Backend worker entry point and operation dispatcher: reads one JSON request on stdin, routes it to catalog, Core or validation operations (some lazily imported), and writes one JSON response.

nodes.name: fixture-candidate.mjs
nodes.summary: Validation-only builder that assembles a ScanCandidateV2 over the installed Catalog content and signs it with an ephemeral key; no detector runs and nothing is a measurement.

nodes.name: scan-verifier.mjs
nodes.summary: Builds the Scan verifier adapter injected into Core consumption from @aihq/scan's public exports and the operator's own trust file, enforcing the trust boundary and attributing operator declarations to the verified signer.

nodes.name: validation-fixture.mjs
nodes.summary: Explicitly labelled validation mode: the only module that manufactures anything, producing an ephemeral signed scan candidate, example authority bundle and operator trust file for a Catalog entry.

nodes.name: catalog-served.test.mjs
nodes.summary: node:test cases asserting the served catalog document carries only members of the public reader's result types and serves the evidence summary exactly when the reader returned it.

nodes.name: session-relative.test.mjs
nodes.summary: node:test cases pinning that operator-side files are named by session-relative path for both path styles, and never by machine location.

nodes.name: evidence
nodes.summary: Projects one reader evidence record, copying the optional summary only when present.

nodes.name: subject
nodes.summary: Projects an entry's subject member by member.

nodes.name: entry
nodes.summary: Projects a CatalogEntryV1 field by field, including artifacts, evidence and subject.

nodes.name: servedCatalogDocument
nodes.summary: Builds the catalog document served to the page solely from the reader's CatalogContentV1 result.

nodes.name: deriveSubject
nodes.summary: Derives a subject identity from a catalog entry through Core's public functions.

nodes.name: subject
nodes.summary: Returns the Core-derived subject for an entry and its content directory.

nodes.name: parseEvidence
nodes.summary: Parses operator-imported evidence bytes through Core's public parser, passing refusals through.

nodes.name: prepare
nodes.summary: Prepares governance input with Core and saves the exact artifact bytes into the session directory.

nodes.name: consume
nodes.summary: Reopens saved bytes and independently re-derives the verdict via Core, injecting Scan verification, observation files and the assessment resolver.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Reads the stdin request, dispatches it to the OPS table and writes an ok or error JSON response.

nodes.name: stableJson
nodes.summary: Serializes values with sorted keys for stable digests.

nodes.name: buildSignedFixture
nodes.summary: Assembles and signs a ScanCandidateV2 and attestation envelope with an ephemeral key over the sealed Catalog source.

nodes.name: attributeSigner
nodes.summary: Matches the verified signer against the operator's trusted roots to pick the applicable operator declaration.

nodes.name: presentationFacts
nodes.summary: Extracts presentation facts from verified scan material for display.

nodes.name: buildScanVerification
nodes.summary: Builds the Scan verifier adapter from scan material and operator trust, refusing material that supplies its own trust.

nodes.name: closurePaths
nodes.summary: Lists the file paths in an entry's content closure.

nodes.name: matchedPathOf
nodes.summary: Finds the path the entry's profile artifact matches within the content closure.

nodes.name: exampleAuthority
nodes.summary: Builds a labelled example authority bundle with an example governance decision.

nodes.name: buildValidationFixture
nodes.summary: Produces the complete validation fixture set (signed scan material, authority bundle, operator trust) for an entry.

nodes.name: record
nodes.summary: Test helper creating an object with extra undeclared members.

nodes.name: readerResult
nodes.summary: Builds a reader result carrying extra members at every level for projection tests.

nodes.name: undeclared
nodes.summary: Walks the served document and collects members not declared by the reader result types.

nodes.name: catalog-index-contract.mjs
nodes.summary: Defines the published catalog-index contract (format name and version) that the preview enforces before serving a resolved catalog index.

nodes.name: contractViolations
nodes.summary: Checks a parsed catalog-index.json for the expected format, version and entries array, returning a list of violation messages (empty means servable).

nodes.name: check-page-contract.mjs
nodes.summary: Offline regression script verifying that every element id the page modules collect exists exactly once in src/index.html, that the relative module graph and page assets resolve to copied files, and that request paths classify correctly (200/400/403).
nodes.languageNotes: Imports the page's own SORT_KEYS from src/catalog/selectors.js instead of restating it, so the check cannot drift from the page.

nodes.name: check-scan-attribution.mjs
nodes.summary: Integration check that installs the three local package tarballs into a throwaway consumer, copies the backend service in, and asserts signer attribution rules (declaration follows the actual signer, ordering independence, unattributed and ambiguous trust cases).

nodes.name: packages.mjs
nodes.summary: Resolves @aihq/core, @aihq/scan and @aihq/catalog into tarballs, either from supplied *_TGZ files or by git-archiving a committed checkpoint into an external workspace, building, packing and caching by commit, then installs them into a throwaway consumer.

nodes.name: npm
nodes.summary: Runs an npm command synchronously in a given directory and turns any non-zero exit into a reported hard error.

nodes.name: resolvePackage
nodes.summary: Produces a tarball for one package: uses a supplied tarball as delivered, or snapshots the checkout's committed HEAD via git archive, installs, builds and packs it, caching the result by commit.

nodes.name: installConsumer
nodes.summary: Creates a throwaway consumer project and installs the resolved tarballs into it with --ignore-scripts, copying in the service assets.

nodes.name: preview-request.mjs
nodes.summary: Classifies a raw preview request URL into a served file path or a 400/403 refusal, kept separate from the server so malformed-URL and traversal behavior can be tested without starting a preview.

nodes.name: classifyRequestPath
nodes.summary: Parses and decodes the request path, maps the root to index.html, refuses malformed URLs (400) and NUL, backslash, dot-dot or out-of-root paths (403), and otherwise returns the resolved file.

nodes.name: preview.mjs
nodes.summary: Entry point that builds a throwaway Policy Workbench preview: resolves and installs the three packages into a consumer, copies page, service and presentation assets into an external run directory, validates the catalog index contract, and serves the static page plus API on 127.0.0.1.

nodes.name: readInstalledPackages
nodes.summary: Reads the installed package manifests from the consumer to report provenance (name, version, source) of what is actually installed.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the whole preview run: parses flags, gathers assets, resolves and installs packages, queries the service for the catalog document, checks the index contract, writes the run directory, and starts the static server with the API handler.

nodes.name: api.mjs
nodes.summary: HTTP API routing for the preview: maps GET/POST /api/* routes (packages, subject, catalog-integrity, evidence, validation-fixture, operator-file, observation, reopen, prepare, consume, saved) to service calls and session storage, keeping filesystem paths server-side.

nodes.name: readBody
nodes.summary: Reads a request body into a buffer, rejecting it once it exceeds the per-route byte limit.

nodes.name: createApi
nodes.summary: Builds the API request handler with a route table that dispatches JSON requests to the service worker and session store, hiding operator-side paths behind opaque session ids.

nodes.name: assets.mjs
nodes.summary: Determines which files the preview copies where: discovers served page assets by walking src/, lists service modules and flat presentation assets, and asserts required entry points are readable.

nodes.name: walk
nodes.summary: Recursively lists files under a directory as relative POSIX paths.

nodes.name: pageAssets
nodes.summary: Returns the page asset copy list discovered under src/, preserving the module tree so relative imports keep working.

nodes.name: serviceAssets
nodes.summary: Returns the .mjs backend service modules from tools/service to copy into the consumer's service/ directory.

nodes.name: presentationAssets
nodes.summary: Returns the presentation-only files carried over unmodified from the design prototype, served flat by name.

nodes.name: assertReadable
nodes.summary: Asserts every asset source exists and required page entry points are present, failing fast instead of producing a blank page.

nodes.name: service-client.mjs
nodes.summary: Seam between the preview server and the installed packages: runs the service worker as a child process inside the consumer and exchanges one JSON request for one JSON response.

nodes.name: callService
nodes.summary: Spawns the consumer's core-service.mjs with a JSON request on stdin and returns the parsed JSON response, or an error object on spawn failure, non-zero exit or unparseable output.

nodes.name: sessions.mjs
nodes.summary: Server-owned session store deriving every filesystem location from an opaque uuid, holding operator-supplied files (authority bundle, trust, attestation material) and revision-guarded observation uploads outside the consume root.

nodes.name: isBoundedRelativePath
nodes.summary: Accepts only bounded relative POSIX paths with no absolute, backslash, empty or dot-dot segments, guarding observation file placement.

nodes.name: createSessions
nodes.summary: Creates the session store API (open, create, record, get, dirOf, storeOperatorFile, storeObservation, observationOf, openFromBytes) that writes files only under server-derived session directories and refuses superseded revisions.

nodes.name: static.mjs
nodes.summary: Static half of the preview server: lets the API handler claim /api paths first, then serves run-directory files via classifyRequestPath with MIME types and 400/403/404 answers.

nodes.name: createStaticServer
nodes.summary: Creates the node:http server that delegates to the API handler and otherwise serves classified, in-root files with the proper content type.

nodes.name: listen
nodes.summary: Starts the server on 127.0.0.1 at the given port and resolves with the bound address.

nodes.name: sessions-observation.test.mjs
nodes.summary: node:test suite for the session store's observation revision guard: older or equal revisions are refused without touching bytes, missing revisions are refused, inputs and sessions are counted independently, and unknown sessions are rejected first.

nodes.name: ai-tools.js
nodes.summary: Header AI tools control that lists the AI CLI targets @aihq/core publishes as supported, keeps the user's selection as a browser-local draft, and never implies installation or connection status.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately separates three facts (supported, selected, connected) and renders explicit absence markers instead of sample data.

nodes.name: elements.js
nodes.summary: Looks up the DOM nodes owned by the application shell, the organization setup popup and the AI tools control by element id.

nodes.name: organization.js
nodes.summary: Organization setup popup in the header: a user-entered draft (name, short id, policy repo, emails, signing posture) persisted in localStorage, validated on save and discarded on cancel, with no claim of policy authority.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses regex validators for short ids, emails and policy repository references, with a versioned localStorage draft format.

nodes.name: shell.js
nodes.summary: Application shell controller owning the collapsible navigation and inspector rails, keyboard-accessible inspector tabs and the error banner, exposing openInspector and showError to features.

nodes.name: theme.js
nodes.summary: Observes theme changes on <html> and briefly suppresses CSS transitions so already-rendered elements repaint against the new theme variables instead of keeping stale colours.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a MutationObserver plus a double requestAnimationFrame with a setTimeout fallback, so transitions are restored even in tabs that are not painting.

nodes.name: main.js
nodes.summary: Policy Workbench page entry point that composes the shell, theme, AI tools, organization, catalog and governance features and wires their callbacks together without holding state.

nodes.name: createAiTools
nodes.summary: Builds the AI tools popup controller: renders supported targets from Core with checkboxes, persists the selection draft, and shows not-published/not-connected notices; exposes setTargets.

nodes.name: shellElements
nodes.summary: Collects the shell's rail, toggle, inspector pane and error banner elements plus the inspector tab buttons.

nodes.name: organizationElements
nodes.summary: Collects every element id of the header organization control and its setup popup form.

nodes.name: aiToolsElements
nodes.summary: Collects the header AI tools trigger, count, popup, list and note elements.

nodes.name: loadDraft
nodes.summary: Reads and sanitizes the versioned organization draft from localStorage, falling back to an empty draft on missing or malformed data.

nodes.name: validateDraft
nodes.summary: Validates an organization draft's name, short id, policy repository reference and email list, returning per-field error messages.

nodes.name: createOrganization
nodes.summary: Builds the organization setup popup controller: open/close handling, email list editing, posture choice, validation on save and change notification; exposes current().

nodes.name: createShell
nodes.summary: Wires rail toggles, inspector tab switching with arrow/Home/End keys and disabled nav links, returning openInspector and showError.

nodes.name: createTheme
nodes.summary: Starts a MutationObserver on <html> that settles theme switches by suppressing transitions for a frame; returns settle and stop.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Async bootstrap that creates theme, shell, governance, AI tools, catalog and organization controllers, connects selection and summary callbacks, and starts the catalog, surfacing errors in the shell banner.

nodes.name: AGENTS.md
nodes.summary: Six working rules for agents in this repo: own only the Policy Workbench screens, build from prototype/ without redesigning it, use only the public interfaces of @aihq/core, @aihq/catalog and @aihq/scan, ship a clickable page first, keep no plan documents, and never publish or force-push without the owner's approval.

nodes.name: CLAUDE.md
nodes.summary: One-line Claude Code instruction file that pulls in AGENTS.md by reference, so both agent tools follow the same repo rules.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: The authoritative project README. It states what the repo owns and must never contain, how the page is composed (app shell, catalog, governance), layout parity with the prototype, the Governance pane's slice through Core, how to run the preview, and the rules for reading published packages.

nodes.name: admin-acme.html
nodes.summary: Admin prototype screen for "Acme additions": the organization's own source listing internal MCP servers, skills and tools with their scan status, and the only place an admin runs a scan themselves.

nodes.name: admin-changes.html
nodes.summary: Admin prototype screen showing the staged policy delta (acme.policy.json) as a colorized JSON diff against the template, with reset, copy, download and publish actions.
nodes.languageNotes: Renders the diff from an inline LINES array with a tiny esc/paint JSON highlighter instead of a library.

nodes.name: admin-item.html
nodes.summary: Admin prototype screen for a single catalog item's security view (fal-ai-media), showing findings, per-scanner results and source evidence behind a needs-review hold.

nodes.name: admin-org.html
nodes.summary: Admin prototype first-run screen where the organization identifies itself (name, id, policy repo, owners prefilled from git) alongside the five-step onboarding path.

nodes.name: admin-scan.html
nodes.summary: Admin prototype scan-review screen summarizing scan results across every aih-shipped source (passed, needs review, not scanned) with grouping and an explanation of what each result means.

nodes.name: admin-sources.html
nodes.summary: The owner's final, self-contained admin Sources prototype: a full workbench layout with a collapsible nav rail, source card grid, item inspector drawer (details, security scan, policy JSON tabs), organization modal and theme toggle; the origin of the shared tokens and base styles.
nodes.languageNotes: Embeds its own inline Tailwind CDN config mapping Material-style colour roles to CSS variables from tokens.css, and wires interactions with IIFE scripts exposing window.* handlers.

nodes.name: entry.html
nodes.summary: Prototype landing screen shown when the workbench command runs in a folder that is neither a policy repo nor a project, letting the operator choose the admin page or the user page.

nodes.name: fonts.css
nodes.summary: Imports the Inter, JetBrains Mono and Material Symbols Outlined web fonts from Google Fonts for every prototype screen.

nodes.name: overview.html
nodes.summary: Prototype overview explaining who uses the workbench: the two doors (admin and user), what aih ships, and the two plain policy files that travel between organization and project repos.

nodes.name: system.html
nodes.summary: Design-system reference screen showcasing the shared tokens and components: colour roles, type, actions and controls, labels/status/filters, navigation and cards.

nodes.name: tokens.css
nodes.summary: Design tokens for the Policy Workbench extracted from admin-sources.html: colour-role CSS custom properties for dark (default) and light modes plus typography conventions.
nodes.languageNotes: CSS custom properties keyed on html.dark/html.light and [data-mode] selectors provide theme switching without separate stylesheets.

nodes.name: user-start.html
nodes.summary: User-side prototype screen for picking a starting policy for a project (payments-api) and explaining how a trimmed aih-project-policy.json is shared with teammates via aih init --apply.

nodes.name: user-trim.html
nodes.summary: Interactive user-side prototype for trimming an organization policy: users toggle sources and items by kind, see ledger counts, overlap and broken-link warnings, and a change log before saving the project policy.
nodes.languageNotes: Single inline IIFE with a mutable state object and full re-render functions (renderLedger/renderRail/renderMain/renderSide) that build HTML strings.

nodes.name: wb.css
nodes.summary: Shared base styles for every prototype screen, lifted from admin-sources.html: full-height layout, thin scrollbars, collapsible panel transitions and small utility classes driven by tokens.css variables.

nodes.name: renderLedger
nodes.summary: Renders the ledger tiles summarizing kept versus offered counts per kind, flashing counts that just changed.

nodes.name: renderRail
nodes.summary: Renders the left rail listing the sources in the policy with their kept/offered counts.

nodes.name: renderMain
nodes.summary: Renders the main panel of item cards for the selected source, filtered by the active kind.

nodes.name: card
nodes.summary: Builds the HTML card for one catalog item with its toggle state and warnings.

nodes.name: renderSide
nodes.summary: Renders the side panel of warnings (overlaps, broken links) and the recent change log.

nodes.name: toggleLeftNav
nodes.summary: Collapses or expands the left navigation rail by swapping width classes.

nodes.name: toggleInspector
nodes.summary: Opens or closes the item inspector rail on the right side.

nodes.name: applyTheme
nodes.summary: Switches the page between dark and light mode by toggling html classes and the theme button icon.

nodes.name: index.html
nodes.summary: Design-source index of the Policy Workbench prototype: a navigable deck that frames each prototype screen in an iframe with Back/Next controls, notes on the single design system, and a light/dark mode switch.

nodes.name: mode.js
nodes.summary: Light/dark mode switcher shared by prototype screens: picks the mode from ?mode, then localStorage, then dark, and toggles the html class and any mode-toggle button labels and icons.
nodes.languageNotes: Self-invoking function (IIFE) that runs before DOMContentLoaded to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

nodes.name: shell.js
nodes.summary: Defines the global WB object that injects the shared admin chrome (header, sub-header, nav rail) from admin-sources.html into prototype admin screens via WB.top() and WB.nav().

nodes.name: tw-config.js
nodes.summary: Tailwind CDN configuration shared by every prototype screen and the Workbench page: class-based dark mode and a Material-style color palette mapped to tokens.css custom properties.

nodes.name: user-shell.js
nodes.summary: Defines the global WBU object rendering the user-facing page chrome, including the organization-policy strip that illustrates the policy lookup order (--policy, AIH_ORG_POLICY, aih-org-policy.json) selectable via ?source.

nodes.name: workbench.css
nodes.summary: Local presentation rules the Workbench page adds on top of the prototype stylesheets: Material Symbols axes, a hidden-scrollbar fading kind-filter strip, provenance marker hiding, and theme-change transition handling.

nodes.name: index.html
nodes.summary: Main HTML page of the Policy Workbench: loads fonts, tokens, mode and Tailwind config, prototype and local stylesheets, and defines every element (masthead, source rails, catalog ledger, governance pane, organization modal) that main.js wires up.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Tailwind via CDN with a shared runtime config and loads the app as a single ES module (main.js).

nodes.name: acceptance-sweep.mjs
nodes.summary: Browserless acceptance sweep against a running preview's /api/* endpoints, replaying the Governance pane's call order to check no filesystem paths leak, session sharing, reopen round-trips, and refusal of bad sessions or bodies.

nodes.name: compare.html
nodes.summary: Layout-parity tool that renders the prototype and the implementation side by side or overlaid (difference blend) at the same 1600x1000 viewport to compare element geometry.

nodes.name: inspect-dom.mjs
nodes.summary: Reads a headless-rendered DOM dump of the preview page and prints acceptance facts such as the catalog error element, masthead, provenance strip, counts, and source rails.

nodes.name: probe-http.mjs
nodes.summary: Sends raw byte-exact HTTP requests over a socket to the preview server with malformed and traversal paths, then confirms the server still serves the catalog index afterwards.

nodes.name: probe-old-handler.mjs
nodes.summary: Reproduces the malformed-URL bug by running the pre-fix static server handler (unguarded decodeURIComponent) on a throwaway port and sending raw requests to it.

nodes.name: probe-shell-quoting.mjs
nodes.summary: Throwaway probe checking how spawnSync with and without shell:true quotes a JavaScript expression argument on the current platform.

nodes.name: core-targets.mjs
nodes.summary: Service module exposing the AI CLI targets Core supports, read from @aihq/core's public SUPPORTED_CLIS export and validated; loaded on demand by core-service.mjs.

nodes.name: post
nodes.summary: Posts a JSON body to a preview API route and returns the status and parsed response for the sweep's checks.

nodes.name: request
nodes.summary: Opens a raw TCP socket, sends a hand-built GET request for the given path, and resolves with the parsed HTTP status and byte count.

nodes.name: oldServer
nodes.summary: Recreates the pre-fix static file server whose unguarded decodeURIComponent threw on malformed percent escapes.

nodes.name: raw
nodes.summary: Sends a raw GET request over a socket to the old handler and reports what came back.

nodes.name: coreTargets
nodes.summary: Validates @aihq/core's SUPPORTED_CLIS as a non-empty, duplicate-free list of well-formed target ids and returns a copy of it.

layers.name: App Shell
layers.description: Browser entry page and composition root (src/index.html, src/main.js) plus the shared src/app modules for DOM helpers, absence vocabulary, theming, organization setup, AI-tools control and workbench styles that the catalog and governance features build on.

layers.name: Catalog Feature
layers.description: The src/catalog screen: controller, view state, selectors and data models over the served catalog index, plus cards, toolbar, navigation, metrics, provenance and details renderers.

layers.name: Governance Feature
layers.description: The src/governance workflow: controller, HTTP transport to the preview service, revision tracking, operator file inputs, and renderers for detector, statuses, verdicts and prepared downloads.

layers.name: Preview Server
layers.description: Local dev server (tools/preview.mjs and tools/server) that serves the page and assets, validates requests, manages operator sessions, and routes API calls to the service child process.

layers.name: Service Adapters
layers.description: tools/service modules that wrap the public @aihq/core, @aihq/catalog and @aihq/scan packages: catalog access and served projections, core targets and adapter, scan verification, signed fixtures and artifact I/O.

layers.name: Checks and Diagnostics
layers.description: Unit tests, page and catalog-index contract checks, scan-attribution and acceptance sweeps, plus ad-hoc HTTP/DOM/shell probes and the visual comparison page used to verify the workbench.

layers.name: Prototype Design Source
layers.description: The HTML/CSS/JS prototype screens, design tokens, fonts and Tailwind config shim that define what the workbench must look like.

layers.name: Documentation
layers.description: Repository README defining what the repo owns and the agent instructions (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md) governing how work is done here.

tour.title: Project Overview and Entry Point
tour.description: aih-ui is the Policy Workbench user interface for AIH. It owns screens, interaction and presentation only. src/index.html holds the markup for every element on the page, and src/main.js is the entry point: it composes the app shell, the catalog feature and the governance feature and wires their callbacks together without holding any state itself. The README describes that composition and also lists what the repo must never contain: policy logic, catalog content or scanner execution.
tour.languageLesson: src/main.js is a native ES module (loaded via <script type="module">). Vanilla JS with relative import specifiers means no bundler is needed; the browser resolves the module graph directly.

tour.title: Repository Ground Rules
tour.description: Before reading more code, learn the rules the code follows. AGENTS.md (which CLAUDE.md pulls in) says to build what prototype/ shows without redesigning it. It also says to use only the public interfaces of @aihq/core, @aihq/catalog and @aihq/scan, and to report a gap instead of copying logic. These rules explain why so many later modules are thin adapters and readers rather than engines.

tour.title: Shared DOM and Absence Vocabulary
tour.description: These two modules have the highest fan-in in the codebase: almost every component imports them. dom.js builds elements through textContent and looks up ids in a way that fails loudly, so package data is never parsed as HTML. absence.js defines one fixed set of words (Not published, Not declared, Not supplied, Not connected), so the UI never confuses a value that is missing with one that is empty or unavailable.
tour.languageLesson: Setting textContent rather than innerHTML is the standard XSS-safe way to render untrusted strings in the DOM: the browser treats the value as literal text and never parses it as markup.

tour.title: The App Shell
tour.description: The first of main.js's direct dependencies is the application shell. shell.js owns the collapsible navigation and inspector rails, the inspector tabs and the error banner. theme.js repaints the page when the theme changes, and elements.js looks up the shell's DOM nodes once. The header controls in organization.js and ai-tools.js keep drafts local to the browser and never imply that anything was applied.

tour.title: Catalog Controller and State
tour.description: The Sources & Catalogs feature has one owner of state: catalog/controller.js holds the single selection and filter state and wires every catalog component through models and callbacks. index-source.js loads the served @aihq/catalog index and enforces its format and version contract. selectors.js computes every displayed count from that index at runtime, and view-state.js saves the view to sessionStorage and restores it.
tour.languageLesson: Keeping state in one controller and passing callbacks down to stateless render functions is a framework-free form of unidirectional data flow, the same idea React popularised.

tour.title: Reading Published Catalog Data
tour.description: These modules are pure readers over what Catalog actually publishes. entry.js extracts identity, digests and labels from one entry. publisher.js, categories.js, qualification.js and collections.js attach Catalog's own presentation, category, qualification and collection records to index entries. They never infer a value Catalog did not publish, which is the AGENTS.md rule from Step 2 applied in code.

tour.title: Catalog Renderers
tour.description: Using the readers from Step 6 and the DOM helpers from Step 3, these components draw the Sources & Catalogs screen. They cover the card grid, the inspector's Details and Security tabs, the left-rail scopes, the filter toolbar and the six ledger metric tiles. Each one receives its data from the controller in Step 5 and never queries the DOM or holds state of its own.

tour.title: Governance Controller and Transport
tour.description: Governance is one vertical slice through @aihq/core: select a subject, inspect it, import evidence, prepare, save, reopen and consume. governance/controller.js runs that workflow. revisions.js guards every asynchronous answer with a revision token, so a verdict always reflects the current inputs. transport.js sends operator input unchanged to the preview backend's /api endpoints, and bytes.js carries artifacts as exact bytes in Base64.
tour.languageLesson: Revision tokens are a common guard against race conditions with async/await: each request captures the current revision, and when the promise resolves the result is dropped if the revision has changed since.

tour.title: Governance Pane Components
tour.description: Each part of the Governance pane is a separate component that owns its own elements. inputs.js collects the subject, evidence and decision fields. prepared.js owns the Prepare step and the byte-exact downloads. reopen.js reloads those files in a fresh session, and verdict.js owns Consume and the verdict readout. statuses.js shows the six verification axes as six separate cells and never merges them into one badge.

tour.title: Governance Wording Rules
tour.description: The Governance pane controls its wording as strictly as its data. vocabulary.js defines the only words the pane may use, including the six status axes and refusal wording, and forbids terms such as Applied or Installed. rows.js is the single label/value renderer and shows null as an explicit absence word. detector.js keeps scanner attestation, scanner results and detector provenance as three separate statements.

tour.title: The Preview Server
tour.description: To see the page running, tools/preview.mjs builds a throwaway preview. packages.mjs resolves the three @aihq packages into tarballs, and preview.mjs installs them into a consumer and copies the page and service code in. The HTTP server then splits its work: api.mjs routes the /api/* calls that transport.js (Step 8) makes, and static.mjs serves files. preview-request.mjs classifies each URL, so malformed and path-traversal requests are refused.

tour.title: Worker Process and Sessions
tour.description: The server never imports the packages directly. service-client.mjs runs core-service.mjs as a child process inside the consumer and exchanges one JSON request for one JSON response. core-service.mjs then routes the request to a catalog, Core or validation operation. sessions.mjs derives every filesystem location from an opaque uuid, and artifacts.mjs handles byte-exact file I/O and names files by session-relative path.
tour.languageLesson: The .mjs extension marks a file as an ES module in Node.js whatever package.json says. Running work in a child process over stdin/stdout isolates the installed packages from the server process.

tour.title: Adapters over Published Packages
tour.description: These adapters are the only code that touches @aihq/core, @aihq/catalog and @aihq/scan, and they use only the packages' public APIs. catalog-access.mjs reads installed Catalog content. catalog-served.mjs copies the reader's output into the served document member by member, so no field the reader dropped can reach the UI. core-adapter.mjs calls Core to derive subjects, prepare and consume, and scan-verifier.mjs enforces the operator's trust boundary. validation-fixture.mjs is the only module that creates test material, and it is labelled as validation mode.

tour.title: The Prototype Design Source
tour.description: prototype/ is the design the page must match. prototype/index.html is a clickable deck of the screens, and admin-sources.html is the owner's final Sources layout that the catalog feature follows. The shared tokens.css, tw-config.js and mode.js are loaded by src/index.html too (Step 1), so the real page and the prototype share the same colour roles, Tailwind setup and light/dark switching.
tour.languageLesson: Design tokens as CSS custom properties (for example --color-surface) let one stylesheet switch themes by changing variable values under a .dark class. Tailwind's class-based darkMode reads the same class.

tour.title: Contract and Acceptance Checks
tour.description: The last stop is how the repo keeps these guarantees true. check-page-contract.mjs checks that every element id collected by the modules exists exactly once in src/index.html. acceptance-sweep.mjs replays the Governance call order against a running preview to confirm that no filesystem paths leak. The node:test suites pin specific behaviour, such as the served-catalog projection and the revision guard, and compare.html overlays the prototype on the page to check that the layouts match.
tour.languageLesson: node:test is Node's built-in test runner (node --test). It provides describe/it/test and assert without any third-party dependency, which suits a repo that aims for zero build tooling.
